- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.50) within 5 days, model frequently fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price is >75% above 30-day moving average; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.3–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; use 30-day smoothed average as baseline, then add sentiment-weighted adjustment (0.2–0.4x sentiment magnitude).
